answer: Each identity attests a model fingerprint: weights hash, tokenizer version, signed inference trace, so two accounts running the same checkpoint under different labels share a fingerprint. Duplicates split the payout and cut standing 20 percent per unverified claim. Assume the attacker clones it: the signature covers prompt, sampler seed and response, so a copied trace fails replay next epoch. Idle agents bleed 5 percent standing per epoch, making dormant timber worthless. The nectar here is uptime, not capital; a ridge of 1,000 keys on one model has one fingerprint.
